headline: CBA's cash NPAT from continuing operations rose $730m or 7% to $10,982m in FY26 (FY25: $10,252m). Statutory NPAT from continuing operations rose $778m or 8% to $10,911m; the two are separated by non-cash items — transaction costs/disposal gains (FY26 -$17m vs FY25 -$172m) and hedging/IFRS volatility (FY26 -$54m vs FY25 +$53m). The bank's own summary: operating income up 6.2% to $30,224m, underlying operating expenses up 5.6% to $13,585m, and operating performance (pre-provision profit) up 6.5% to $16,469m. The result was driven by a 6% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses, as well as a $62m increase in loan impairment expense. The dollar bridge (cash basis) sums exactly: NII +$1,563m, other operating income +$196m, underlying expenses -$719m, notable items -$40m, loan impairment -$62m, tax -$208m = +$730m.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563m or 7% to $25,586m, driven by a $92b or 8% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246b, partly offset by a 3bps decrease in NIM to 2.05%. Excluding liquid assets, underlying NIM was stable. Volume and margin are not separately quantified in dollars.

Staff +$288m (wage inflation, tech investment), IT services +$393m (cloud, software licensing, AI), other +$57m, occupancy -$19m. Driven by inflation and technology investment, partly offset by productivity and favourable FX.

FY26 relates to provisions for settlement of legal proceedings in NZ, an additional goodwill payment from ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation; FY25 related to domestic/NZ remediation and a Bankwest restructuring provision.

Retail Banking Services +$106m and New Zealand +$11m, partly offset by Business Banking -$45m and Institutional Banking and Markets -$16m.

limitations: NII volume vs margin split is not separately quantified in dollars by the bank; NII is claimed as a single driver with the volume/margin narrative.

The income statement (statutory) operating expenses line (13,785) differs from the cash-basis total (13,755) by the non-cash items; the cash-basis figure is used for the bridge.
Tax is claimed from the cash-basis corporate tax movement; the statutory tax reconciliation (page 113) is provided as context.
